# SDD — POC-03: Dialectical Reframing Engine ("8 positions of the cube")

**Status:** Pre-registered POC | **Effort:** 1–2 weeks | **Priority:** 3 of 4
**Falsifiable question:** Do algebra-grounded reframes — exactly 8 views generated by the cube's real operators (3 single-line flips, 3 double-flips, 1 complement via Hodge dual) — produce reframes that are measurably more diverse than LLM free-form reframes while staying coherent?

## 1. Pre-registration (before any code)

| Item | Commitment |
|------|------------|
| Primary claim (automated proxy) | Mean pairwise semantic distance of the 8 algebra-grounded views ≥ LLM free-form reframes + **0.15** (cosine on 8-dim rubric vectors, same encoder both arms), AND mean coherence (LLM-judged, 1–5) ≥ 3.5 |
| Human gate (manual, later) | ≥70% of raters rate the algebra-grounded set "more systematically complete" than the free-form set (n≥5) — pre-registered, run after the proxy passes |
| Benchmark | 20 input statements across 4 domains (product claims, policy statements, scientific hypotheses, design decisions) — frozen before any run |
| Protocol | Arm A: LLM free-form "give 8 alternative framings". Arm B: calculator generates the 8 moves → LLM names each position (one call per position). Same model, temperature 0 |
| Kill criterion | Proxy claim fails → POC-03 dies as a claim (moves remain useful only pedagogically → Path C, not a product) |
| Honesty | The 8 moves are REAL operators (no free-form); naming quality is the only LLM variable; per-position naming failures counted, not retried |

## 2. Scope

**In:** calculator moves (flip ×3, double-flip ×3, complement ×1) over trigram states; LLM naming protocol (position description → name/reframe, JSON); diversity metric (mean pairwise cosine on rubric vectors of the resulting statements); coherence metric (LLM-judged 1–5, averaged); benchmark (20 statements); runner (Arm A vs Arm B); reports; tests.
**Out:** No claim that the reframes are "true"; no semantic derivation; no retrieval.

## 3. Architecture

```
statements.py   20 input statements (frozen)
moves.py        the 8 operators over trigram states (bit-level, exact)
naming.py       LLM: position state + move → named reframe (JSON)
metrics.py      diversity (mean pairwise cosine), coherence (LLM 1–5)
run_all.py      Arm A (free-form) vs Arm B (algebra-grounded) → output/ + verdict
```

## 4. Interfaces

| Component | File | Interface |
|-----------|------|-----------|
| Moves | `moves.py` | `all_positions(state) -> list[(move_name, state)]`; `flip(state, line)`, `complement(state)` |
| Naming | `naming.py` | `name_position(statement, move_name, state) -> str` |
| Metrics | `metrics.py` | `diversity(statements) -> float`; `coherence(statement, reframes) -> float` (LLM judge) |
| Runner | `run_all.py` | both arms, mean metrics, paired comparison, verdict |

## 5. Evaluation protocol

1. Statements frozen; both arms run on the same 20 statements, same model/temperature.
2. Arm A: one LLM call per statement returning 8 reframes (JSON array). Arm B: 8 moves × 1 naming call each.
3. Diversity: encode all reframes with the rubric encoder (Path D protocol) → mean pairwise cosine within the set → arm mean.
4. Coherence: LLM judge scores each set 1–5 (one call per set); mean per arm.
5. Paired comparison on the 20 statements (diversity delta, coherence delta); verdict per pre-registration.
6. Token ledger appended; deterministic caching.

## 6. Acceptance criteria (TDD: `docs/tdd/poc-03-tdd.md`)

- AC-03.1 all_positions returns exactly 8 distinct states for every trigram; flips/complement exact (bit-level)
- AC-03.2 complement = Hodge dual under natural convention (Kan→Li, Gen→Dui, …) — the coherent identity
- AC-03.3 naming protocol parses/validates; failures countable
- AC-03.4 diversity metric correct (hand-computed pair)
- AC-03.5 coherence metric returns 1–5, deterministic on cached responses
- AC-03.6 runner renders arm comparison + verdict rows
- AC-03.7 determinism + ledger + tests green
